text: ## PR description ### [BugFix] Use KV cache scale mapper in custom loaders [labels: ready] ## Purpose Resolves #4809 Fix custom model loaders that still call the removed vLLM `get_cache_scale` API after vLLM PR #43167 (`62215e72c`). That upstream change first landed in vLLM `v0.23.0rc2` / `v0.23.0` and vLLM-Omni picked it up in PR #4286 (`7b837944`), the vLLM 0.23.0 rebase. Without this fix, affected quantized checkpoints can fail during weight load: ```text AttributeError: '' object has no attribute 'get_cache_scale' ``` This updates the affected model-executor loaders to use the new KV-cache scale mapper path, or rely on the outer `AutoWeightsLoader` when applicable. Changes by loader: - **Hunyuan-image AR**: removed the manual `get_cache_scale` branch. This loader is reached through an outer `AutoWeightsLoader`, so KV-cache scale names are already mapped before the custom loader handles them. - **MammothModa2 AR**: applies `quant_config.get_cache_scale_mapper()` before iterating weights. This loader is called directly and therefore must perform the mapper step itself. - **MiMo-Audio LLM**: applies `quant_config.get_cache_scale_mapper()` before iterating weights for the same reason as MammothModa2: it bypasses the outer `AutoWeightsLoader` path. - **Qwen2.5-Omni old Qwen2 loader**: removed the old guarded `get_cache_scale` fallback. The parent model loads through `AutoWeightsLoader`, so keeping a second cache-scale path is redundant and depends on a removed API. Related issue: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/4806 ## Test Plan - Add CPU regression coverage for loaders that must not call the removed `get_cache_scale` API. - Verify direct custom loaders apply `get_cache_scale_mapper()`. - Verify delegated loaders accept already-mapped KV-cache scale names. ## ENV: vLLM Version : 0.24.0 vLLM-Omni Version : 0.1.dev2107+ga560ed184.rocm (git sha: a560ed184, date: ocm) ## Test Result I added a small CPU-based regression test for the API change as demonstration; Will remove it from the PR once this is validated by a maintainer as I don't think this coverage is necessary!
